title: Federated SLI pool and initiative playbook for cross-team reliability commitments
creator: Ava Kim
description: Create a repeatable playbook and lightweight system for federating SLIs across related services into a pooled error-budget that initiatives can draw from. The goal is to allow product and platform teams to coordinate reliability investments (canary rollouts, capacity buys, throttles) against a single pooled runway while keeping per-service ownership and observability. Deliverables: policy model, calculation rules for normalizing SLIs, Console UI sketch for pooled view, automation recipes for gating deployments when pooled burn exceeds thresholds, and runbook for stewardship rotation.
background: Multiple product teams today maintain independent SLIs and error budgets; initiatives that span services (eg. embeddings pipeline + realtime API) lack a unified mechanism to coordinate trade-offs.
Current ad-hoc pooling (Slack threads + spreadsheets) causes duplicated work and inconsistent gating decisions during high burn events.
We need a defensible, auditable approach that preserves per-service SLI fidelity while enabling initiative-level commitments and automatic enforcement where appropriate.
goals: Define a normalization method so heterogeneous SLIs (p99 latency, success rate, token failure rate) can be expressed on a common scale for pooling.
Deliver Console prototype showing pooled error budget runway and per-service contribution breakdown.
Ship automation recipes: soft-throttle (alert + PR), hard-throttle (rate limit route), and rollback gating tied to pooled thresholds.
Publish stewardship rotation playbook and oncall handoff template for pooled initiatives.
acceptance_criteria: Normalization spec reviewed and approved by SRE + Product (documented formulas and edge-cases).
Console prototype (mock + interactive) demonstrates pooled runway, per-service weights, and projected depletion under an incident scenario.
Automation chore 'pooled-gate' merged (ENG) that evaluates pooled burn and emits a standardized decision event and Slack alert to owners.
Simulation run shows initiative-level gating would have reduced prior incident blast-radius in at least 2 historical case studies.
milestones: M5: Publish guide + secure stewardship rotation (2026-04-30)
notes: 2026-02-15: Kickoff with SRE, Platform, and Product—initial alignment on need for pooled runway for multi-service initiatives.
2026-02-22: Chose z-score based normalization to convert heterogeneous SLI metrics into comparable burn units; alternative (percentile scaling) retained as fallback.
2026-03-01: Engineering raised concern about telemetry fidelity for newly onboarded services; added ENG-45998 to dependencies.
2026-03-10: Design reviewed Console mock; requested clearer breakdown of contribution and an explainer for how weights are computed.
2026-03-12: Decided automated hard-throttle will be opt-in per-initiative and require steward sign-off; default remains soft-fail (alerts + rollback recommendations).
decision_log: 2026-02-22: Adopt z-score normalization to allow error budgets to be pooled while preserving distributional characteristics of each SLI.
2026-03-12: Automation gating default will be soft; hard gating requires steward roster enrollment and product acceptance criteria.
2026-03-14: Weighting by customer-impact and traffic share chosen vs equal-weight; final formula includes tunable factors.
risks: Incorrect normalization could bias pooled allocations toward noisy SLIs and lead to unfair throttles.
Insufficient telemetry coverage from new services will produce inaccurate runway projections.
Teams may resist pooled stewardship if they perceive a loss of control over their own error budget.
mitigation_plan: Add minimum telemetry quality gates (SLO exporter coverage, sampling rate) as preconditions for joining the pool.
Run a three-month pilot with two initiatives and a rollback path; evaluate stakeholder satisfaction and incident outcomes.
Provide visibility controls and per-service opt-out within the pooled view to preserve autonomy.
next_steps: Finish normalization spec and circulate for SRE review (due 2026-02-26).
Prototype Console mock as interactive Figma + small React demo for PMs by 2026-03-12.
ENG to wire telemetry hooks for pilot services (ENG-45210 assignee to triage).
Schedule pilot steward rotation and oncall playbook dry run in April.
